subject: Post-demo: FastCart throughput probe + next actions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom@fastcart.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FastCart throughput probe + next actions

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary from demo:
- Primary flow: cart checkout NLP for line-item extraction + offer personalization. Typical payload ~600 tokens; streaming not required for most calls but a small fraction (~5%) are interactive UI flows where streaming latency matters.
- Current expectation: 95th-pct latency target ≤ 350ms for synchronous checkout calls; occasional background batch enrichment can tolerate higher latency.
- Throughput: baseline 120 QPS for checkout endpoints; peak windows ~1,200 QPS for Black Friday-like spikes (10x baseline) lasting 10–20 minutes.

Asks / immediate next steps:
1) FastCart to share a 24–48h sample of production traffic (anonymized): token counts, arrival timestamps, and concurrency per-minute. If possible, CSV or JSON lines. (Attached is a small example format we use.)
2) Redwood to run a lightweight probe with a synthetic mix based on that sample to confirm slot sizing and burst handling. I attached the probe instructions and a short checklist for your infra team.
3) Confirm streaming needs: if you need tail-streaming for the 5% interactive flows, we’ll include streaming concurrency targets in the probe.
4) Schedule a 30-min ops sync next week to review results and capacity recommendations.

Attachments: fastcart_workload_sample.csv (format example), redwood_probe_instructions.pdf

I'll loop in Ben and Monica for sizing and follow-up. Thanks —
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Tom Li <tom@fastcart.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@fastcart.ai>, ops@fastcart.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FastCart throughput probe + next actions

Thanks Rachel — super helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Payloads: the 600 tokens is accurate for checkout ML calls; the interactive UI paths average ~120 tokens but are sensitive to first-byte latency.
- Arrivals: our traffic has clear bimodal peaks (weekday business hours and evening surge), and the Black Friday-like scenario is what we worry about — past analytics show the 10x crest can last up to 25 minutes.

We can share a 48h anonymized export. Ops will scrub PII and push to the Drive link you shared. Expect that by Monday EOD PST.

Quick Q: for the probe, do you need us to route traffic through a staging endpoint or can we run the probe from Redwood-hosted load generators? We prefer the second option initially to avoid touching staging certs.

—Tom
Product Lead, FastCart
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom@fastcart.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FastCart throughput probe + next actions

Looping in technical notes and my proposed probe plan below. Marking action items.

Ben's probe plan (high level):
- Phase A (baseline): Redwood-hosted load generators simulate 10 minutes at baseline (120 QPS) with payload distribution matching sample; measure p50/p90/p95 latency and token throughput.
- Phase B (crest): Simulate a 10/20/25-minute crest at 10x baseline; repeat with varying concurrency windows to exercise autoscaling and queueing.
- Phase C (streaming sample): For the 5% interactive flows, run a streaming scenario with 200 concurrent streams and measure end-to-end first-byte latency and sustained concurrency.

Specifics we need from FastCart (action items):
A1) 48h anonymized traffic export (tokens, timestamp, route, status).
A2) Confirmation if routing probe from Redwood is acceptable (we can run non-prod load generators from us-east and us-west).
A3) Any per-customer rate limits or connection limits we should respect.

Deliverables from Redwood after probe:
- Sizing recommendation (slots, pre-warm, burst allowance) with expected 95th-pct latency and cost delta by mode (hosted vs dedicated).
- Short runbook for your ops with config snippets for canary and fallback.

Attachments included: none. I'll prepare the probe configuration once we get the CSV.

—Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

- No per-customer rate caps beyond standard API limits; we will provide expected burst window start times based on our marketing calendar so you can tune crest tests.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: FastCart throughput probe + next actions

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample export, Samir. Next steps on our side: 

1) Ben + Monica will run an initial probe using Redwood-hosted load generators on Wed 2026-12-02 (us-east and us-west windows). We will only hit a Redwood staging endpoint and use whitelisted IPs you provide.
2) We'll run Phase A today (baseline) and Phase B (crest) on the 2nd, then share results in a concise runbook and a 30-min review slot the same day.
3) If streaming first-byte latency for the interactive flow misses your 95th-pct target, we'll propose a dedicated small pool to serve that path (tradeoff: slightly higher cost for guaranteed tail latency).

Proposed 30-min review: Wed 2026-12-02 15:00 PST — does that work for you? If so, we'll send a calendar invite and attach the probe results and config.

Thanks again — Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
